# Tic-tac-toe: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script (pilot)

**Runnable.** `tic-tac-toe.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `tic-tac-toe-rules.soar` (23 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). `run.py` is the environment: it plays blue. Needs Soar 9.6.6 or a 9.6.50 build.

## Run

    python3 run.py 1 --games 10

## Opponent (decided 16 Nov 2026)

The dialog teaches only red's move, red's goal and the losing condition. The environment plays blue with random legal moves under the same move rule as red's, red moves first, and the environment checks every red move for legality and signals the end of the game. Blue's moves reach the agent on the input-link (`^opponent-move`, `^turn`, `^blue-moves`, `^game-over`); task rules copy them onto the state (IO-019), apply them to the world, and let red propose a move only when the environment says it is red's turn and every blue move has been applied (IO-021). The agent halts on the environment's end-of-game signal (IO-022). Look-ahead covers red's own moves only, so the agent does not block blue's threats.

## Results (Soar 9.6.50, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states | init: goal false, failure false; final-tictactoe2rc: goal true; fail-tictactoerc: failure true |
| 10 games against random blue (seeds 1-10) | red wins 9, blue wins 1 (seed 2: red did not block); 505-609 decisions per game; no illegal red move; the agent's own success or failure matched the environment's result in every game |
| Settings probe | not run: the probe harness has no opponent. Library defaults |

## Assumption ledger

| ID | Statement | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| A-T1 | 4, 6 | "clear" applies to blocks as well as locations: only the top block of each stack can move (as A-H1). |
| A-T2 | 12, 14 | "three of the captured locations are in a line": three different locations that are members of one of the 8 lines of the predicate-set linear. |
| A-T3 | (none) | Red moves first; turns alternate (environment). |
| A-T4 | 4 | The action has no name in the dialog; it is called `move`. |
| A-T5 | (none) | The game is a draw when neither side has a legal move; the dialog has no draw. |

Convention notes: `available` and `clear` are maintained one-argument relations; `captured`, `occupied` and `in a line` are expanded in place; each line is a world object with a static `member` relation. One deviation: the application of a move by a block that sits on nothing (the bottom of its stack) tests the absence of an on relation, a local negation in a look-ahead application (W-CHK-009, Should). Chunking is off, so it has no effect now.
